Starting values that keep the sampler out of the flat regions

Source: R/cogmod_inits.R
cogmod_inits.Rd

Builds an init argument for brms::brm(), for the custom families whose default starting point is a bad one.

This is not a tuning knob to reach for when sampling looks bad. For the families with a non-decision time the default start is actively harmful, and the failure is silent: the chain does not error, it simply never moves.

Usage

cogmod_inits(formula = NULL, data = NULL, jitter = NULL, warmstart = NULL, ...)

Arguments

formula

The model formula, as passed to brms::brm(). Must carry the family, i.e. be built with brms::bf(..., family = cogmod_gamma()). May be left NULL only when warmstart is a brmsfit, whose formula is then used.

data

The data, as passed to brms::brm(). May be left NULL only when warmstart is a brmsfit, whose data are then used.

jitter

SD of the noise added on the unconstrained scale, so that chains start at different points. One number sets the population-level blocks (intercepts and slopes; for a slope, divided by how far its design columns reach) and a fifth of it the group-level and smooth blocks (z_*, zs_*, sd_*, sds_*), where a unit of noise is multiplied through a scale and a design column, once per group or basis function. Two numbers set the two tiers, population first. 0 gives identical starts. NULL (the default) means 0.25, or 0.05 with a warmstart, whose values come from a converged posterior.

warmstart

A previous fit to start from instead of the family's generic values: a brmsfit, a cogmod_warmstart() object, the data frame as.data.frame() makes of one, or the path to a CSV file of it. The starting values are its posterior means, mapped onto this model by parameter name (a pilot on fewer participants included; see cogmod_warmstart()); whatever it has no value for keeps the value this function would give it anyway.

...

Passed to brms::make_stancode() and brms::make_standata(), for arguments such as data2.

Value

A function of one argument, suitable for brms::brm(init = ). Each call returns a named list of starting values, one for every parameter the generated Stan program declares.

Details

Two regions of the parameter space have no gradient to escape on, and both are easy to start inside.

  • ndt too large. brms initialises on the unconstrained scale, so init = 0 puts ndt at exp(0) = 1 second, above nearly every sub-second response. Every response is then attributed to the outlier component, the decision parameters drop out of the density, and their gradient is exactly zero.

  • Shape below 1. For cogmod_gamma() and cogmod_weibull() the density is unbounded at ndt whenever the shape is below 1, and init = 0 starts a softplus shape at log(2) = 0.69, inside that region.

No single scalar init avoids both - ndt = exp(c) wants c around -1.6, shape = softplus(c) wants it above 1.9 - so the parameters have to be set separately, which is what this function does.

How it works

The parameter declarations are read off brms::make_stancode() for the model you are fitting, and their dimensions off brms::make_standata(), so 0 + Intercept, interactions, group-level terms and smooths are matched however brms names and sizes them. Every declared parameter gets a value, which also spares you CmdStan's message about a partial list:

  • The family's values go to the intercept of each distributional parameter, on its link scale - through the links on the family, so cogmod_gamma(link_mu = "log") is honoured - and, on the natural scale, to any parameter left out of the formula, which brms declares as a plain auxiliary parameter. Under 0 + Intercept the value goes to the coefficient named Intercept.

  • ndt starts at half the first percentile of the observed response times: below essentially every response, but on the data's own scale. The two errors are not symmetric: a start too small only means the shift has to grow, which the gradient does, while one too large removes the gradient.

  • The error accumulator of cogmod_rdm(), cogmod_lba2() and cogmod_lnr() starts slower than the correct one (driftone = 1 against mu = 3, nuone = 0 against mu = 0.7): few data sets are a 50/50 race, and for the Wald and the LBA a start too fast costs far more than one too slow. Each family's page has the details.

  • Everything else gets a generic value at least as good as Stan's own U(-2, 2): zero for slopes and standardized effects, just above the bound for a positive parameter, the midpoint for a doubly bounded one, the identity for a Cholesky factor. A smooth's SD (sds) starts where its smooth is nearly flat, at 0.1 link units of wiggle, a different value on every basis; see Smooth terms in cogmod_priors().

Each chain gets a different draw. The noise is added on the unconstrained scale, so a value can never leave its bounds. For a regression coefficient it is divided by the largest row norm of the coefficient block's design columns, wherever that exceeds 1, so that at no row does the SD of what reaches the linear predictor exceed jitter: a slope on age in years would otherwise start with an SD of six link units at the oldest participant.

Supported families

The family is read off formula, so build it with brms::bf(..., family = cogmod_gamma()). The families are those of cogmod_priors(), listed in its Supported families section: every family with an ndt + poutlier component; cogmod_exgaussian() and cogmod_geg(), whose parameters are lengths of time that the default start puts at 0 s or 0.69 s; and the rating-scale families cogmod_choco(), cogmod_betagate() and cogmod_betadiscrete(), where it describes a scale nobody uses - half the responses on the midpoint or at an endpoint, or a U-shaped Beta. Any other family is an error.

See also

cogmod_priors(), cogmod_stanvars(), cogmod_warmstart()

Examples

d <- data.frame(RT = rcogmod_gamma(50, ndt = 0.3, poutlier = 0.02))
f <- brms::bf(RT ~ 1, sigma ~ 1, ndt ~ 1, poutlier ~ 1, family = cogmod_gamma())
inits <- cogmod_inits(f, d)
inits(1)
#> $Intercept
#> [1] 1.477312
#> 
#> $Intercept_sigma
#> [1] -1.124586
#> 
#> $Intercept_ndt
#> [1] -2.349416
#> 
#> $Intercept_poutlier
#> [1] -3.861294
#> 

# The rating-scale families are covered too. `pmid` starts at 0.05 rather
# than the logit origin's 0.5, which would put half of every response
# exactly on the midpoint of the scale.
r <- data.frame(y = rcogmod_choco(50, pmid = 0.05))
g <- brms::bf(y ~ 1, pmid ~ 1, family = cogmod_choco())
cogmod_inits(g, r, jitter = 0)(1)
#> $Intercept
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $confright
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $precright
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $confleft
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $precleft
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $pex
#> [1] 0.1
#> 
#> $bex
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $Intercept_pmid
#> [1] -2.944439
#> 

# \donttest{
# Fitting needs cmdstanr, which lives outside CRAN - see the package website.
if (requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE) &&
    !is.null(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(error_on_NA = FALSE))) {
  m <- brms::brm(f,
    data = d, prior = cogmod_priors(f, d),
    stanvars = cogmod_stanvars(f), init = cogmod_inits(f, d),
    backend = "cmdstanr", chains = 1, iter = 500, refresh = 0
  )
}
# }
